title: Thematic seasonality pilot — sakura cohort
candidateDefinition: 341 cohort = state unknown + no season/bestMonths + at least one audit likelyProfile; sakura pilot = exact intersection whose likelyProfiles includes sakura. The signal is only a research lead.
scopeDecision: Mutate only 14 non-hub records with authoritative month-level evidence; preserve hubs, broad/ambiguous evidence, lexical false positives, and all other cohorts.

records.name: Arakurayama Sengen Park & Chureito Pagoda

seasonMetadata.basis: no rule matched; owner policy: unknown stays unknown

thematicSignal.description: Japan's iconic postcard panorama featuring the five-story Chureito Pagoda framing Mount Fuji surrounded by cherry blossoms.

officialEvidence.authority: Fujiyoshida Tourism Promotion Service, official Fujiyoshida City tourism guide
observations: The page says the view is especially notable during the spring cherry-blossom season, while the landscape changes through spring, summer, autumn, and winter. Opening hours are listed as 24 hours.

records.decision: 24-hour access and spring cherry scenery are official, but no month window; retain unknown numeric fields.

records.name: Awa Shrine

seasonMetadata.basis: Operational hours and seasonal openings do not establish a defensible four-season suitability score; unknown is preserved.

highlights: A large white torii and wooded approach to the main sanctuary
Cherry blossoms along the approach in early April

observations: “If you have a chance, come visit in early April, when cherry trees along the approach are in full bloom.” The same page lists regular shrine hours of 8:30am–5pm; it does not explicitly state year-round opening.

records.decision: Official page explicitly says approach trees are in full bloom in early April.

records.name: Goryokaku (Star Fort)

seasonMetadata.basis: no rule matched; owner policy: unknown stays unknown

highlights: Site of the 1869 Battle of Hakodate
Spring cherry blossoms and night illumination

observations: The official spot page lists park use times for both 4–10月 and 11–3月, supporting continuous year-round park access. It says the fort turns cherry-pink around the May Golden Week period. The official cherry feature states: “五稜郭公園のお花見は、例年4月下旬から5月中旬まで。”

records.decision: Official Hakodate sources document year-round access and late-April-to-mid-May cherry viewing.

records.name: Hirosaki City

seasonMetadata.basis: hub records span multiple microclimates; single vector would be fabricated

thematicSignal.description: A former castle town best known for Hirosaki Castle and one of Japan's most celebrated cherry-blossom festivals.

officialEvidence.authority: Hirosaki Tourism and Convention Association, official tourism body

records.decision: Official tourism association gives April 10-May 5, but this is a city hub and remains vectorless.

records.name: Ichijodani Castle (Asakura site)

seasonMetadata.basis: no rule matched; owner policy: unknown stays unknown

thematicSignal.name: Ichijodani Castle (Asakura site)
thematicSignal.description: Ichijodani was the 15th-16th century castle town of the Asakura clan, Japan's most fully excavated Sengoku city, designated a special historic site. The castle ruins crown the valley, with the town's garden sites preserved below.

observations: The official seasonal-scenery page has separate Spring, Summer, Autumn, and Winter sections; the spring image labels include Ichijodani scenery and cherry blossoms. No bloom month or peak window is stated.

officialEvidence.authority: Fukui Prefectural Tourism Federation, official Fukui tourism site
observations: The official attraction page includes image labels for spring/cherry scenery and states that the archaeological site itself is open for free viewing. No concrete cherry-blossom period is given.

records.decision: Official pages show spring/cherry scenery but no defensible month window.

records.name: Kagoshima Castle

seasonMetadata.basis: no rule matched; owner policy: unknown stays unknown

officialEvidence.authority: Kagoshima City official tourism information site, Kagoshima Yokanavi
observations: The official spring-flowers feature has a section titled “Pink cherry blossoms and Kagoshima Castle’s Goromon gate” and says visitors can encounter beautiful cherry blossoms at the gate. The castle spot page lists daily illumination from sunset to 22:00, but neither page gives a cherry-blossom month or bounded peak window.

records.decision: Official spring material confirms cherry blossoms but gives no month window.

records.name: Kagoshima City

seasonMetadata.basis: hub records span multiple microclimates; single vector would be fabricated

thematicSignal.description: Southern coastal city known as 'Naples of Japan', facing active Sakurajima volcano across Kagoshima Bay.

officialEvidence.authority: Kagoshima City official tourism information site, Kagoshima Yokanavi
observations: The city-wide spring feature says cherry blossoms can be enjoyed in Kagoshima City. Its component attractions have different windows: Sengan-en has successive cherry varieties from early February through early April; Yoshino Park has Kawazu cherry blossoms from mid- to late February and Somei Yoshino from mid-March through early April. The Kagoshima Castle section gives no month.

records.decision: Component attractions have different windows; no single hub vector is justified.

records.name: Kakunodate Samurai District

seasonMetadata.basis: no rule matched; owner policy: unknown stays unknown

officialEvidence.authority: Semboku City official tourism information / municipal government
observations: Semboku City's seasonal recommendations place Kakunodate weeping cherry blossoms from mid-April to early May. The district page separately documents seasonal opening periods for individual samurai residences; it does not establish year-round access for every facility.
角館のシダレザクラ（4月中旬～5月上旬）

records.decision: Semboku City states mid-April to early May for Kakunodate weeping cherry blossoms.

records.name: Kimii-dera Temple

seasonMetadata.basis: no rule matched; owner policy: unknown stays unknown

observations: The temple states it has about 500 cherry trees and is famous for early-blooming cherry blossoms. Its 2026 official updates record mountain cherry blooming on March 15, the Somei-Yoshino sample tree opening on March 24, full bloom on April 2, and late double-cherry viewing on April 12. Regular worship/reception hours are documented as 08:00–17:00, but no explicit year-round opening claim was used.
早咲き桜の名所；3月も半ばとなると…

records.decision: Temple pages document early blooming plus March-April observations.

records.name: Kintaikyo Wooden Arch Bridge

seasonMetadata.basis: no rule matched; owner policy: unknown stays unknown

observations: The official summary describes cherry blossoms in spring as the bridge's most beautiful season and states the bridge can be crossed 24 hours. Official bloom reports recorded full bloom on March 29, 2013, and April 3, 2014, establishing a March–April seasonal peak while distinguishing it from year-round bridge access.
春は桜…春は一年で最も美しい季節です；24時間入橋は可能

records.decision: Official bridge material documents 24-hour crossing, spring scenery, and March/April full-bloom observations.

records.name: Kirishima-Kinkowan National Park

seasonMetadata.basis: no rule matched; owner policy: unknown stays unknown

thematicSignal.description: National park (1934) of the Kirishima volcano group with its crater lakes, and the Sakurajima peninsula and Kinko Bay coast of southern Kyushu.

officialEvidence.authority: Japan Ministry of the Environment official national park site
observations: The official overview identifies the park's Kirishima volcanic massif, Kinko Bay, and Sakurajima and describes visitor areas and activities. The retrieved official pages do not provide a cherry-blossom bloom window, sakura-specific event period, or month-level seasonal peak. The park name/volcanic Sakurajima reference was not treated as sakura-season evidence.

records.decision: Sakurajima place-name signal only; official park pages provide no sakura timing.

records.name: Kita City

seasonMetadata.basis: hub records span multiple microclimates; single vector would be fabricated

thematicSignal.description: A northern Tokyo ward known for Asukayama Park's cherry blossoms, historic paper museum, and Akabane's bar culture.

officialEvidence.authority: Kita City official tourism site / Kita City Regional Promotion Department
observations: The official evidence establishes a spring cherry peak for Asukayama Park, a component attraction of the Kita City ward aggregate, including mid-April viewing of later-blooming double cherries. It does not establish a defensible single seasonal window or vector for the entire hub; the hub season-model guard therefore remains in force.
現在も桜の名所として、毎年春には多くの人が訪れます。…4月中旬には「御衣黄」「福禄寿」などの八重桜も楽しめます。

records.decision: Evidence concerns component Asukayama Park, not a city-hub window.

records.name: Matsumae Castle

seasonMetadata.basis: no rule matched; owner policy: unknown stays unknown

thematicSignal.description: Matsumae Castle, completed 1854, was the northernmost castle of the Edo-period Matsumae domain and the only castle in Hokkaido. The current keep is a 1961 concrete reconstruction (the original burned in 1949); it is famous for its early-spring cherry blossoms.

observations: Matsumae Town states that the cherry festival is held in Matsumae Park surrounding Matsumae Castle from late April to mid-May. The same page documents 250 varieties and more than 10,000 trees, with early-, mid-, and late-blooming varieties extending flowering for more than one month. No year-round castle-access claim was used.
4月下旬～5月中旬にかけ、松前城周辺に広がる松前公園で開催される「さくらまつり」

records.decision: Matsumae Town gives late-April-to-mid-May and staggered varieties.

records.name: Meguro City

thematicSignal.description: A trendy riverside ward famous for Meguro River cherry blossoms, stylish boutiques, cafes, and Tokyo Metropolitan Teien Art Museum.

observations: Meguro City identifies cherry-tree-lined walks along the Meguro River and says many flower-viewing visitors arrive during cherry season. The official pages provide no concrete month-level window, and the evidence concerns component river walks rather than the entire Meguro ward hub; no hub vector is proposed.
桜の季節には、多くの花見客が訪れる；桜並木が続きます。

records.decision: Municipal pages confirm cherry-lined walks but no month window for the ward hub.

A 10-minute ferry ride from Meinohama to the island

records.name: Odawara Castle

seasonMetadata.basis: no rule matched; owner policy: unknown stays unknown

thematicSignal.description: Odawara Castle was the mighty stronghold of the Hojo clan that withstood sieges until Hideyoshi's 1590 campaign. The current keep (1960) houses a museum; the castle park is famous for plum and cherry blossoms.

observations: The official annual flower calendar lists 桜 as 2～4月, including 河津桜 2月上旬～3月上旬, ソメイヨシノ 3月下旬〜4月中旬, 大島桜 4月上旬, and 枝垂れ桜 3月下旬～4月上旬.

records.decision: Official flower calendar documents cherry varieties from February through April.

records.name: Okazaki Castle

seasonMetadata.basis: no rule matched; owner policy: unknown stays unknown

thematicSignal.description: Okazaki Castle is the birthplace of Tokugawa Ieyasu (1542), built by his grandfather's generation of the Matsudaira clan. The 1959-reconstructed keep overlooks the Yahagi river; the grounds are a famous cherry-blossom park.

officialEvidence.authority: Okazaki City Tourism Association, official Okazaki tourism site

records.name: Serigaya Park

seasonMetadata.basis: no rule matched; owner policy: unknown stays unknown

thematicSignal.description: A lush valley park in Machida featuring natural springs, woodland walking trails, and a unique kinetic sculpture fountain. It is a popular spot for family picnics, cherry blossom viewing, and outdoor play.

officialEvidence.authority: Machida City; Machida City Tourism Guide
observations: Machida City page updated 2026-09-01 states the park is open every day year-round (年中無休).
Machida Tourism Guide report dated 2026-03-25: Somei Yoshino at the south-gate cherry tunnel was three-to-five-tenths in bloom; other park areas ranged from three-tenths to nearly seven-tenths.
Machida Tourism Guide report dated 2026-04-06 for the 2026-04-05 observation: south-gate cherries were beginning to fall but were still beautifully in bloom.

records.decision: Machida City and tourism association document year-round opening and March-April observations.

records.name: Tama Forest Science Garden

seasonMetadata.basis: no rule matched; owner policy: unknown stays unknown

officialEvidence.authority: Forestry and Forest Products Research Institute, Tama Forest Science Garden
observations: Japanese official cherry page published 2026-04-01: varieties peak sequentially from late February through late April (2月下旬から4月下旬にかけて順次見頃).
English official passport page states cherry trees blossom successively from the second half of March through the end of April.
Japanese official passport page states successive blooming from the latter half of March through the end of April (3月後半から4月末).
Official admissions page states the garden is open every day in March and April but closes every Monday during much of the rest of the year and during December 26-January 6.
officialEvidence.evidenceDate: 2026-04-01 page update and undated official pages; checked 2026-09-02

records.decision: Official Japanese and English pages give different cherry start ranges; do not guess.
